title: Cut paper
when: Title sequences, openers, podcast and series intros, posters in motion: bold flat shapes in rhythm
rules: Flat shapes in two or three colours: no gradients, glows or lens effects. The edge of a cut is the texture.
Shapes become each other across cuts (the same element id in consecutive canvas beats morphs): a disc becomes a bar, which becomes a door. Continuity is the whole grammar.
Type is condensed caps with wide tracking, set into the composition like another shape, never as a caption.
Cut on the music: every beat is one move and one hold. Let the negative space do half the work.
Asymmetry and diagonals: nothing sits dead centre unless it is the title.
